To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel model that jointly estimates depth and semantic segmentation from RGB image.

1) we propose a novel model for simultaneous depth and semantic estimation; 2) we show the feasibility of training a model for multiple tasks by fine tuning the model on all tasks; 3) we demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the state of the arts methods on semantic segmentation; 4) we show that our model achieves comparable results to the state of the arst methods on depth estimation
1) We present a novel deep learning model for joint semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of joint semantic segmentation and depth estimation using a single deep CNN.

the following questions: Can a deep convolutional neural network trained on a single task be reused to solve another task, such as depth prediction? Can the performance of such a network be further improved using fully connected CRF? Can a single network trained on both tasks outperform a network trained on each task individually?

the following questions: (a) How can we train a single model for multiple tasks using a shared representation and a single loss function? (b) How can we use contextual information for joint semantic segmentation and depth estimation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is able to perform joint semantic segmentation and depth estimation from a single RGB input image.
the proposed model is able to learn both tasks jointly, while improving the performance of the individual tasks compared to training each task separately.
the proposed approach is a significant step towards a unified solution for simultaneous depth estimation, semantic segmentation and contextual reasoning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be used for simultaneous depth estimation, semantic segmentation and joint inference of the two.
it is the first time that the two tasks have been solved jointly with a unified loss function.
we present a new architecture for depth estimation and semantic scene segmentation from a single image.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model can be trained from scratch or fine-tuned from a pretrained semantic segmentation network and can be used as a generic framework for joint depth estimation and semantic labelling.

it is possible to learn a single model that is able to perform both tasks, depth estimation and semantic segmenation, with a single loss function and that the final performance is superior to training the two tasks independently.
a deep network can be trained for multiple tasks and that fine tuning the network on both tasks simultaneously leads to a better performance on both tasks.
